title: On the Absence of Identifiable Manifolds in Finite-Max Composite Optimization
summary: In nonsmooth optimization, identifiable sets describe the local region eventually reached by sequences converging to a prescribed critical point. When such a set is a $C^2$ manifold on which the objective restricts to a $C^2$ function, it is called an identifiable manifold. Their appeal lies in what they enable: many first-order methods identify these manifolds in finitely many iterations, after which the iterates enter a region in which the problem is effectively smooth. Consequently, many powerful tools and guarantees from smooth optimization transplant naturally to the nonsmooth setting.…
